title: A flow-cytometry-based protocol for detection of mitochondrial ROS production under hypoxia
protocol: Passage cells at log phase during which the cells are actively dividing, healthy and ≥ 90% viable.
Discard culture medium from cells.
Gently shake cell bottle and discard dead or poorly adherent cells.
Add preheated trypsin-EDTA (0.25%) to cells and hold at approximately 18°C–25°C until cells become shrunk and round, typically after 3 to 5 minutes.
Neutralize trypsin-EDTA by adding preheated complete medium in a volume twice that of the trypsin-EDTA used.
Count cells using hemocytometer or automated cell counters such as CountStar system.
Seed cells into 6-well plate at density of 3 to 7 × 10^5 cells/well, depending on doubling time.
Add medium to a final volume of 2 mL per well.
Incubate the seeded cells in a normoxic CO2 incubator for 12 hours.
Change the cell culture media to 1750 μL fresh media with FBS per well.
Dilute 2.5 μg plasmid in 125 μL Opti-MEMTM media within a 1.5 mL tube (Tube 1).
Add 5 μL P3000TM from LipofectamineTM 3000 Kit into Tube 1.
Dilute 3.75 μL LipofectamineTM 3000 in 125 μL Opti-MEMTM media in another 1.5 mL tube (Tube 2).
Incubate at almost 18°C–25°C for 10 min.
Add the plasmid-p3000TM mixture in Tube 1 to Tube 2.
Add plasmid-Lipofectamine 3000-p3000TM mixture into the well.
Divide the cells into the hypoxic group and the normoxic group based on oxygen levels required for the experiment.
Place the hypoxic group in an incubator set to 1% O2, 5% CO2, and 94% N2.
Place the normoxic group in an incubator set to 21% O2, 5% CO2, and 74% N2.
Limit the frequency and duration of door openings during hypoxic treatment.
Ensure cells return to stable hypoxic environment as soon as possible after door openings.
Observe transfected cells under a fluorescence microscope to estimate confluence.
Prepare 5 mM MitoSOX reagent stock solution.
Place each MitoSOX vial at approximately 18°C–25°C before opening.
Centrifuge the MitoSOX vial at 1000 g for 1 min.
Dissolve the contents (50 μg) of one vial in 13 μL DMSO to make a 5 mM solution.
Collect normoxic cells with 1 mL preheated medium without serum or HBSS into flow cytometry tubes.
Digest adherent cells with preheated trypsin-EDTA for 3–5 min.
Wash cells three times with preheated medium/HBSS or hypoxia-pretreated medium.
Centrifuge cells each time at 400 g for 3 min at approximately 18°C–25°C.
Count cells using a hemocytometer or automated cell counters and adjust to a concentration of 1–5 × 10^6 cells per mL in the corresponding medium.
Add 1 μL of MitoSOX stock solution to each cell suspension to make a 5 μM MitoSOX reagent working solution.
Shake gently.
Dilute cells at a density of 5 × 10^6 cells/mL before staining.
Store the remaining working solution at 4°C in a refrigerator, protected from light for up to one week.
Prepare one tube of cells as a negative control by adding the same amount of DMSO.
Incubate the cells for 20 min in a normoxic or hypoxic incubator, protected from light.
Incubate cells with MitoSOX for 15-30 minutes at 37°C.
Preheat buffer to 37°C before use.
Wash cells gently three times with preheated medium/HBSS or hypoxia-pretreated medium.
Centrifuge the cells at 400 g for 3 min at approximately 18-25°C during washing.
Prepare cells for flow cytometry.
Quantify MitoSOX expression in the PE channel by flow cytometry.
